N’hésitez plus et rejoignez le CEA !

Pour le développement de réacteurs à l’échelle micro-millifluidique, les méthodes de modification de surface des matériaux employés sont un point crucial pour contrôler la mouillabilité qui conditionne la dynamique des fluides. Une méthode de référence consiste à greffer de façon covalente des molécules organiques sur les surfaces exposées aux fluides.

Dans le cadre de ce stage, les compétences de deux laboratoires, l’un spécialisé en traitements de surfaces et en synthèse organique et l’autre en génie chimique seront associées. Il s’agira de modifier l’hydrophilie des surfaces internes de réacteurs, en verre ou en plastique, afin de contrôler les interactions fluide-paroi.

Il est proposé d’évaluer le traitement de surface de verre ou de plastique en deux étapes : Une étape d’activation radicalaire pour former une couche d’accroche réactive vis-à-vis de greffons organiques, une étape de greffage covalent d’un composé organique en surface du matériau.

Une évaluation de la modification des propriétés de surface sera conduite pour déterminer si les modifications moléculaires apportent une solution pertinente aux problématiques de mouillabilité.

La pérennité et la résistance du traitement pourront aussi être étudiées.

Le stagiaire utilisera un laboratoire équipé pour la synthèse et purification de composés organiques ainsi que des moyens analytiques pour le suivi de réaction et la caractérisation des molécules synthétisées, et des moyens de caractérisation de surfaces.

Vous intègrerez les équipes de l’Institut des Sciences et technologies pour une Economie Circulaire des énergies bas carbone – ISEC.

added.description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join the Specialist Antimicrobial Chemotherapy Unit (SACU) in Cardiff, delivering specialist services and supporting bacteriology laboratories throughout Wales.

SACU is the antimicrobial resistance reference service for Wales, providing resistance mechanism detection, specialist antimicrobial susceptibility testing support, and therapeutic guidance to laboratories across the Welsh microbiology network.

Alongside our reference laboratory services, we collaborate with academic institutions and commercial partners across Europe, acting as the central laboratory for clinical trials and research studies. These projects focus on antimicrobial resistance, infection management, and reducing unnecessary antibiotic use in primary care through the application of SACU's expertise in microbiology and resistance detection. The unit also supports the evaluation of novel antimicrobials and the validation of new diagnostic and commercial products.

The successful candidate will join a supportive and innovative team where full training and mentorship will be provided. We are committed to professional development and will encourage and support you to develop specialist skills.

As part of a friendly and experienced team, you will help support the detection, investigation and monitoring of antimicrobial resistance across Wales.

As a Band 6 Biomedical Scientist, you will carry out a range of antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) methods, including disc diffusion, gradient strip MIC testing and broth microdilution. You will interpret results in line with EUCAST guidelines and contribute to the laboratory's growing molecular service, using techniques such as real-time PCR and whole genome sequencing (WGS).

You will also help maintain the laboratory's UKAS ISO 15189:2022 accreditation by taking part in quality activities, including internal quality assurance (IQA), external quality assessment (EQA) and audits.

We are looking for someone who is enthusiastic, organised and keen to learn. A flexible approach, good practical laboratory skills and the ability to work well as part of a team are important. You will be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to service improvements and play an active role in delivering a high-quality service for laboratories across the Welsh Microbiology Network.

– the national public health agency in Wales. Our purpose is ‘ Working together for a healthier Wales' . We exist to help everyone in Wales live longer, healthier, happier lives. Together with our partners, we work to increase healthy life expectancy, improve health and well-being, and reduce inequalities for everyone in Wales, now and for future generations.

Our teams work to prevent disease, protect health, and provide leadership, specialist services and public health expertise. We are the leading source of public health information, research and innovation in Wales. In a world facing complex health challenges, our work has never been so important.

Help build the evidence for better health and care for people experiencing homelessness. We are seeking a compassionate, organised and motivated Clinical Research Practitioner to join our Research and Development team and support delivery of the REACH trial.

REACH is a multi-centre clinical trial funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR). It evaluates whether integrated health, housing and practical support improves the health, wellbeing and social outcomes of people experiencing homelessness who live in temporary accommodation, compared with usual care. The intervention provides support for up to 12 months, using trauma-informed and strengths-based principles.

You will play a key role in identifying and recruiting participants, coordinating study visits and maintaining engagement throughout follow-up. Working closely with the REACH research and intervention teams, homelessness services, temporary accommodation providers and wider health and social care partners, you will help deliver high-quality research addressing inequalities in care and access to services.

You will manage an allocated participant caseload and organise research activities autonomously, with support from the Research Delivery Manager and study team. The role combines participant-facing work in clinical and community settings with study coordination, accurate data collection and research governance.

Work with clinical services, homelessness teams and accommodation providers to identify, screen and recruit eligible participants through approved pathways.
